locator.section: Dawn Postcommunion and the reference for St Anastasia. The cited revision resolves the reference to C6b (Præsta nobis). C6a supplies the separate Satiásti reading in the transcription. The Mass Ordo supplies both conclusions.

entries.claim: The dawn Mass gives its own Postcommunion and a reference for St Anastasia. The reference calls for the prayer Præsta nobis in the Common. The digital transcription follows another prayer in the Common, Satiásti, which also appears under St Anastasia in the 1962 printed Missal.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Per Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented conclusion with no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses nostrum through Deus.; the cue words Per Dóminum come from p. 20, and this page supplies neither the final duration nor Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion, ending with Amen. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 b; mention of the Son at the beginning of an oration

entries.claim: RG 115 b prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc. ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. This Postcommunion speaks of the Nativity in its body (cuius Natívitas singuláris humánam répulit vetustátem), not of the Son at its end; the composite follows the printed cue. The end-mention rule in 115 c is not used here.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 116; other particular conclusions noted in the liturgical books

entries.claim: RG 116 keeps the particular conclusions the liturgical books note. This Postcommunion names the birth in its opening clause (nóvitas natális) and the Nativity in its body (cuius Natívitas singuláris), and does not name the Son, so the condition of RG 115 b is met only through the Nativity; page 20 prints Per eúndem Dóminum., and the printed cue controls.
